newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Columbia River hydropower dam flows rising.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Columbia River hydropower dam flows rising.

text.p: Flows at Chief Joseph Dam on the Columbia River in Washington State are forecast to rise to an average 180,000 to 188,000 cubic feet per second (cfs) over the next week, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers said Thursday.
Flows from Chief Joe, just downstream of Grand Coulee, had been averaging around 140,000 cfs but were over 210,000 cfs at 1300 PDT on Thursday, the Corps said.
Flows were forecast to average 176,000 cfs on Friday, 183,000 cfs on Sunday, 182,000 cfs on Monday and 188,000 cfs on Tuesday.
"I think we are right at the tip of the beginning of the melt," said a source at the Corps' reservoir control center in Portland, Oregon.
"It might blip back down for a short time, but this looks like it," she added.
The Corps earlier this week requested limits on discharges from Grand Coulee, the uppermost U.S. project on the Columbia, due to concerns about downstream flooding.

But Coulee's end-of-month reservoir target level is 1,208 feet, compared with a current level of 1,216 feet, so more space will need to be cleared in the reservoir, the Corps and other industry sources said.
As of 1300 PDT on Thursday, flows from Grand Coulee were running at 203,000 cfs, compared with a limit of 140,00 cfs imposed earlier in the week.
